chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who sells me silver (dirhams) for gold (dinars), and I weigh from it and weigh for him until I finish, and there is no transaction between me and him except that in his silver there are weak (coins), counterfeit ones, and what is not permissible, so he says, 'Check them and return the weak ones.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in it, but do not delay that for more than one day or two days, for it is essentially exchange (sarf). I said, 'And if I find in his silver an excess equal to the amount of the weak (coins) in it?' He said: 'This is precaution (ihtiyat); this is more beloved to me (peace be upon him).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on delaying the settlement of a gold-silver exchange to sort out defective coins?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits the exchange of silver for gold with a delay for sorting out defective coins, provided the delay does not exceed two days. He further advises that if the excess value of the good coins equals the deficit of the bad ones, it is a recommended precaution (ihtiyat). This ruling highlights the practical application of 'sarf' (currency exchange) in early Islamic commerce, addressing the common issue of debased currency.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said, 
‘I asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> about the man who sold me the silver (Dirhams) with the Dinars, and I weighed from it.

So I weighed for him until I was free, and there was no work between me and him except regarding his silver (Dirhams) were spoilt and weak (coins) and what is not allowed (invalid coins). So he said, ‘Cash these and return the invalid ones’. 
فَقَالَ لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ وَ لَكِنْ لَا تُؤَخِّرْ ذَلِكَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ يَوْمٍ أَوْ يَوْمَيْنِ فَإِنَّمَا هُوَ الصَّرْفُ قُلْتُ فَإِنْ وَجَدْتُ فِي وَرِقِهِ فَضْلًا مِقْدَارَ مَا فِيهَا مِنَ النُّفَايَةِ فَقَالَ هَذَا احْتِيَاطٌ هَذَا أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ .

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no probem with it, but you should not delay that for more than one day or two days, for this, rather is the exchange’. I said, ‘Supposing if he were to find in his silver (dirhams) excess of the measurement of whatever was therein from the invalid (coins)?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a precaution. This is more beloved to me<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who sold to me wariq (dirham) for dinar and I weighed it from him. I weighed it for him until it was complete and there was no other work between us, except that his wariq (dirham) had invalid and unreal pieces, and what was not permissible in them. He asked me to find and return such pieces.

He (the Imam) said, Tt is not unlawful; however, you must not delay it more than one day or two, because it is exchange . 5 I then asked, ’What happens if I find extra in them equal to the amount of invalid ones ? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘This is precautionary measure and I like it more . 555
